name: Thaddaeus
overview: Thaddaeus was a male disciple of the Messiah and one of the Twelve Apostles chosen by Christ, as recorded in Matthew 10:3. His role as a follower of Jesus places him among the foundational witnesses to the ministry of the Lord. Scripture identifies him explicitly as one of the Twelve, underscoring his importance in the early Christian community.
namesAndTitles: This disciple is known primarily by the name Thaddaeus, as stated in Matthew 10:3. He is also referred to as Judas, a name meaning 'praised,' according to Luke 6:16. These names indicate the same individual, although the meaning of Thaddaeus is not provided in the text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Thaddaeus was the son of James, as noted in Luke 6:16. Beyond this familial link and his relationship as a disciple and apostle of YHVH, no further family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Thaddaeus is significant as one of the Twelve Apostles personally chosen by Jesus Christ, marking him as a key figure in the foundation of the Church. His inclusion among the Twelve highlights his role in bearing witness to Christ’s teachings and mission. The dual naming as Thaddaeus and Judas reflects the biblical practice of individuals having multiple names or titles, which can signify different aspects of their identity or ministry.
